verdict.summary: You can create a Xero app with a free account and connect your own organisation in minutes, with no review. The limit is connections: uncertified apps get 5 connected organisations on the free Starter tier, or 50 on the paid Core tier. Going past 50 means passing Xero certification, which needs ten customers by Xero's own figure and is repeated every year. Advanced and Enterprise tiers also require a security assessment.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min to reach a working connection; days to weeks of work to meet the certification checkpoints
verdict.approval_wait: None for up to 5 (Starter) or 50 (Core, paid) connections. Xero does not publish a certification timeline.

gates.unlocks: Other users can connect their organisations. Starter allows up to 5 connected organisations. The paid Core tier allows up to 50, with no certification.

gates.name: Certified app (Plus, Advanced or Enterprise tier)
gates.unlocks: 1,000 connections on Plus or 10,000 on Advanced (reported), with Enterprise on application. Removes the per-organisation 5-uncertified-app cap and makes an App Store listing possible.
limits: Certification is required for Plus, Advanced and Enterprise.
Advanced and Enterprise also need an initial and annual security assessment.
Certification is repeated every year. Xero may suspend an app that stops meeting the requirements.
An App Store listing needs Plus or above and is mandatory only on Enterprise.
gates.time_to_reach: Weeks or more. You need ten customers before certifying (Xero's figure), and Xero publishes no review timeline.

steps.title: Sign in to the Xero developer portal
steps.detail: Create a free Xero user account if you don't have one, then sign in at developer.xero.com and open My Apps (app/manage). Community guides say a free account is enough to create an app.
gotchas: The portal is rendered with JavaScript, so you have to use a browser. Scripted page reads won't show the form.

steps.title: Prepare a company URL and privacy policy URL
steps.detail: The New app form asks for a company URL and a privacy policy URL. An agent can draft a privacy policy page covering the Xero data your agent reads and writes, and check that both URLs load.
gotchas: A community wiki reports that Xero's developer terms forbid using API data to train AI models. Say so in the policy if it applies to you.

steps.title: Create a new Web app
steps.detail: Click 'New app'. Enter the app name, set the integration type to Web app (the standard code flow for servers that can keep a client secret), and enter the company URL and privacy policy URL. Accept the terms and create the app.
gotchas: Xero does not currently support single-page apps. PKCE is meant for mobile and desktop apps. Composio needs the Web app (client secret) type.

steps.title: Register the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: In the app's redirect URI field, paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio Xero auth config. Composio's default is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The URI must be absolute and match letter for letter. Wildcards are not accepted.
An app can have up to 50 redirect URIs.

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and generate a Client Secret
steps.detail: On the app's configuration page, copy the Client ID, generate a Client Secret and store both securely. Composio has no managed Xero app, so you need these credentials.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config with granular scopes
steps.detail: Create a Xero OAuth2 auth config in Composio using your Client ID and Secret. Keep granular scopes such as accounting.invoices.read and offline_access, and trim the list to what your agent needs. Apps created on or after 2 March 2026 use granular scopes only.
gotchas: Requesting the deprecated broad scopes accounting.transactions or accounting.reports.read from a new app has been reported to fail with invalid_scope.

steps.title: Run a test authorisation with your own organisation
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio, sign in to Xero, choose your organisation and approve. Then make a read call, for example list contacts, to confirm that tokens and scopes work.
gotchas: 'unauthorized_client: Unknown client or client not enabled' means the Client ID is wrong or the app isn't set up correctly.
The authorization code is single-use and expires after 5 minutes.

steps.title: Keep refresh tokens alive
steps.detail: Access tokens last 30 minutes. Each refresh returns a new refresh token that replaces the old one, and refresh tokens expire after 60 days without use. Refresh idle connections on a schedule so users don't have to re-authorise.
gotchas: If a refresh response is lost, you can retry with the previous refresh token for up to 30 minutes.

steps.title: Connect test organisations within Starter limits
steps.detail: Invite testers to connect their organisations. Starter allows 5 connected organisations, and multiple users on the same organisation count once. Watch the 1,000 calls per day per organisation limit.
gotchas: An organisation that already has 5 uncertified apps connected cannot connect yours.

steps.title: Upgrade to Core for up to 50 connections
steps.detail: When you need more than 5 organisations, move the app to the paid Core tier in the developer portal. Core allows 50 connections without certification and is reported at $35 AUD per month.

steps.title: Meet the certification checkpoints
steps.detail: Prepare the integration against Xero's certification checkpoints: connection, branding and naming, app launcher, scopes (including offline_access), error handling, data integrity, account and payment mapping, and taxes. Add Sign Up with Xero, which is required for certification. An agent can implement and document these items.

steps.title: Apply for certification
steps.detail: Once you have the required customers (ten, according to Xero's Grow with Xero page), apply for certification. Xero gives you the detailed requirements and the recertification process when you apply.

steps.title: Wait for the certification review
steps.detail: Xero reviews the app. No official timeline was found for this review.

steps.title: Choose a certified tier and keep it current
steps.detail: Move to Plus, Advanced or Enterprise. Advanced and Enterprise need an initial and annual security assessment. An App Store listing needs Plus or above and is required only on Enterprise. Recertify every year to avoid suspension.

scopes.effect: Returns a refresh token (60 days if unused). Required for certification and for long-running agents.
OpenID identity scopes. The Sign Up with Xero variant requests these only.
Granular replacements for accounting.transactions. Apps created on or after 2 March 2026 must use these. Scopes are reviewed as part of certification.

blockers.cause: The app was created after 2 March 2026 and requests broad scopes such as accounting.transactions.
blockers.fix: Request the granular scopes instead, for example accounting.invoices.read.

blockers.symptom: 'unauthorized_client: Unknown client or client not enabled'
blockers.cause: The Client ID is wrong, or the app is not registered or enabled.
blockers.fix: Copy the Client ID again from developer.xero.com/app/manage into the Composio auth config.

blockers.symptom: Redirect URI mismatch error during login or token exchange
blockers.cause: The callback doesn't exactly match the URI registered on the app, or a wildcard was used.
blockers.fix: Register the exact Composio callback URL as an absolute URI.

blockers.symptom: New organisations can't connect after the 5th
blockers.cause: The Starter tier connection cap for uncertified apps.
blockers.fix: Upgrade to Core (50 connections) or get certified for higher tiers.

blockers.symptom: A specific customer's organisation can't connect your app
blockers.cause: That organisation already has 5 uncertified apps connected.
blockers.fix: The customer disconnects another uncertified app, or you get certified.

blockers.symptom: Users are asked to re-authorise after a period of inactivity
blockers.cause: The refresh token went unused for 60 days, or a rotated refresh token was not saved.
blockers.fix: Store each new refresh token and refresh idle connections regularly.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Xero, so you must create your own Xero Web app and enter its Client ID and Secret. Register Composio's callback (default https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add) as the redirect URI. The default scopes are already granular, which new Xero apps require. Trim them to what your agent needs.

evidence.claim: Composio reports no managed OAuth app for Xero; its OAUTH2 auth config uses Composio's callback as the default redirect and lists Xero's authorize and token URLs.

Apps created between 4 December 2025 and 2 March 2026 wanting App Store publication start on an interim billing solution.
Uncertified apps default to Starter with five connections; Core raises it to fifty; App Store listing needs Plus or above.
Each Xero organisation can connect to at most five uncertified apps.
Only one connection per organisation counts toward the app's limit.
Per-tenant limits: 5 concurrent, 60/min, 1,000/day on Starter or 5,000/day higher; 10,000/min app-wide.
Xero's developer terms reportedly prohibit using API data to train AI models.
Annual recertification is required for Plus or above; missing it risks temporary App Store removal.
Xero may suspend an app if it stops meeting certification requirements.
Specific certification requirements, including recertification, are given to the applicant on application.

open_questions: No official Xero page lists the exact app-creation form fields, or says whether a paid plan or business verification is needed first. Community sources say a free account is enough.
No official review timeline for certification was found.
The certification entry threshold conflicts: Xero says ten customers, a third-party guide says three. Confirm on Xero's application form.
It's unclear whether a privacy policy, logo, demo video or listing copy is required at certification. The checkpoints page body could not be read.
The tier caps and rate limits were read from search snippets of the limits page. Re-check them on the live page.
It's unconfirmed whether Xero assigns the files and projects scopes from Composio's default list to a new app. Check in the portal.
Plan prices come from a community wiki, not Xero's pricing page.
